newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends below 8,000 points on new signs of stronger growth.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends below 8,000 points on new signs of stronger growth.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average staggered lower Tuesday, ending below the 8,000 point level for the first time in three weeks on new evidence that economic growth is accelerating from its tame second quarter pace.
Based on early and unofficial data, the Dow was off 101.27 points, or 1.2 percent, at 7,960.84, its first close below the 8,000 level since July 21.

The economic news, which came in the form of a stronger than expected weekly report on the nation's retail sales, dealt a severe blow to the already jittery bond market, which is bracing for a critical monthly sales report on Wednesday.

"People are aware of the potency of (tomorrow's) retail sales number," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "They know that a couple of months of buoyant retail sales could change the Fed's mood."
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond slumped 14/32, and the yield jumped to 6.68 percent from 6.64 percent at Monday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Among the big movers, Amgen Inc. tumbled 6-15/16 to a year low of 50-3/16 after it warned of reduced earnings expectations for its key Epogen drug.
